description:
FILED s459an (agent AN, round 16), found by the #870 corpus run: 270 of 3864
checks disagreed with real perl, all in one direction, all answering 0.  The
cause was NOT version.pm -- it was the SWAP idiom version.pm used.

REPRO (perl / PCL):

    my $x = [1,2];
    my $y = [9];
    ($x, $y) = ($y, $x);
    print scalar(@$x), ",", scalar(@$y), "\n";   # perl 1,2   PCL 1,1

    my @a=(1,2); my @b=(3,4,5);
    my ($ra,$rb) = (\@a,\@b);
    ($ra,$rb) = ($rb,$ra);
    print scalar(@$ra), ",", scalar(@$rb), "\n"; # perl 3,2   PCL 3,3

The PLAIN-SCALAR swap is CORRECT (`my $p="P"; my $q="Q"; ($p,$q)=($q,$p)`
gives QP), and so is the swap of two sub PARAMETERS.  It is REFERENCE values
that collapse: both names end up holding what the FIRST assignment stored.

MECHANISM, located.  `p-list-=` binds its RHS through `%p-flatten-list`
(cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), NOT through `%p-assign-snapshot-vector` -- which is
what `p-array-=` and `p-hash-=` and the p-setf slice arms use.  And
`%p-assign-snapshot`'s own docstring names THIS case as the reason it exists:
"perl evaluates the WHOLE right-hand side of a list assignment before any
store happens ... `($a,$b) = ($b,$a)` (the same variable box on both sides)".

But its rules keep the LIVE BOX for a reference:

    - p-box with a box inner (a reference) -> keep the outer box
    - blessed / array-ref / hash-ref / dualvar box -> keep the box

so even routing p-list-= through the snapshot would not fix it: `box-set $y
<live box of $x>` reads $x AFTER $x has already been overwritten.  Keeping the
box is presumably there to preserve the is-ref / class flags on the CONTAINER
(the same reason the typeglob arm exists) -- and the typeglob arm shows the
answer: it returns a FRESH box carrying `p-box-is-ref`, precisely because
"keeping ITEM would alias -- ($g1,$g2) = ($g2,$g1) collapsed to one glob"
(#423).  The array-ref / hash-ref / blessed / dualvar arms need that same
treatment, and p-list-= needs to call the snapshot vector at all.

TWO CHANGES, then, and they are both in the box model:
  (1) `p-list-=` uses `%p-assign-snapshot-vector` like its aggregate siblings;
  (2) `%p-assign-snapshot`'s reference arms return a FRESH box with the same
      inner value and the same is-ref/class flags, as the typeglob arm does.
Probe (2) against ref IDENTITY first -- `$r1 == $r2`, `refaddr`, `\$x == \$x`
-- since it changes which BOX carries a reference, and against the #818 slice
case the docstring names.

WHY NOT FIXED IN s459an: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp's aggregate/box region belongs to
the sibling agent this round.  lib/version.pm was written in perl's own
non-swapping idiom instead (`return $swap ? -$res : $res`), which is both
correct and independent of this bug.

BAR: the two repros above, `($g1,$g2)=($g2,$g1)` (the #423 shape, must not
regress), a swap of two blessed objects, a swap of a ref and a plain scalar,
`($a,$b,$c)=($c,$a,$b)`, and the full sweep -- p-list-= is on every list
assignment path, so this is a sweep-is-the-gate change.


=== SHIPPED s460ap (agent AP, round 17).  #891 CLOSED.

WHAT THE FIX IS.  ONE rule in ONE place: %p-assign-snapshot's container arms
return a FRESH box (%p-container-snapshot) carrying the same inner value and the
same container flags -- class, is-ref, and a dualvar's cached NV/SV -- exactly
as the typeglob arm already did for #423.  The typeglob arm is now that same
call, so there is one copy rule, not two.

THE TASK'S CHANGE (1) WAS NOT NEEDED, AND THAT IS A FINDING.  `p-list-=` ALREADY
snapshots: it binds its RHS through %p-flatten-list, whose scalar fall-through
arm calls %p-assign-snapshot (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the `t` arm of the `add`
labels).  So p-list-= and the p-setf slice arms were already reading the same
rule -- the whole bug was (2).  Routing p-list-= through
%p-assign-snapshot-vector as well would have been a second walk over the same
vector for no behaviour change.

THE FAMILY IS WIDER THAN THE TASK'S REPRO, measured before the fix (32 probe
rows vs perl 5.40.3, two files).  Diverging: array-ref, hash-ref, blessed,
SCALAR-ref (`($r1,$r2)=($r2,$r1)` then `$$r1`), mixed ref/plain, 3-cycle
rotation, array-ELEMENT swap `($e[0],$e[1])=($e[1],$e[0])`, hash-element swap,
sub-parameter swap, AND the two SLICE self-swaps `@a[0,1] = @a[1,0]` /
`@h{qw(x y)} = @h{qw(y x)}` when the values are refs -- the slice arms run
%p-assign-snapshot-vector, which reads the same rule, so they had the same bug.
NOT diverging (and unchanged): plain scalars, CODE refs (a function is not a
box, so it reduced to a bare value one arm down), typeglobs (#423).

INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION FROM PERL'S OWN SUITE.  perl-tests/multideref.t test
42 "OA_DANGEROUS b" is literally
    my $x = {}; $x->{a} = [1]; $x->{b} = [2];
    ($x->{a}, $x->{b}) = ($x->{b}, $x->{a});
under the comment "test that multideref is marked OA_DANGEROUS, i.e. it's one
of the ops that should set the OPpASSIGN_COMMON flag in list assignments".  It
was a blessed baseline FAIL and now passes: sweep TOTAL 18340 -> 18341, GATE
clean, 0 new / 0 fixed elsewhere, drops 5 = census.  multideref.t 42/10 -> 43/9,
verified against a base-runtime single-file run (row 42 fails there, every other
row byte-identical); both baselines edited ROW BY ROW with the cause.

WHAT IT COSTS, MEASURED (flagged per the standing "flag any bugfix that slows
execution" rule).  The standard bench table does NOT move -- gcdrec 0.0939 ->
0.0913, arrfill 0.0717 -> 0.0712, slices 0.2125 -> 0.2119, sliceasgn 0.0529 ->
0.0535, ovlsub 0.1318 -> 0.1344, packunpk 4.379 -> 4.387 (best-of-3, all within
run-to-run spread) -- because no bench row list-assigns a REFERENCE.  The cost
is one struct allocation per reference element that passes through a list
assignment, and a deliberately worst-case micro-bench pays it:
    sub add { my ($self,$x,$r) = @_; ... }   # blessed + array-ref per call
    4e6 calls: base 2.13 s exec, fixed 2.32 s exec  = +8.9 %
So OO code whose methods start `my ($self, ...) = @_` with reference arguments
pays up to ~9 %.  Correctness won here (a silent-wrong on every reference swap),
and the OPTIMIZATION IS FILED AS #910: perl itself only copies when the
assignment is "common" (OPpASSIGN_COMMON, set by the peephole optimizer), and
p-list-= knows its LHS target symbols at MACRO EXPANSION time, so an
allocation-free `eq`-scan against the remaining src-vec would recover the whole
9 % in the common case.  Do NOT do it by narrowing %p-assign-snapshot alone --
the slice arms read the same rule and would silently regress (probed).

GUARD: Pl/t/aassign-01.t rows 37-40 (36 -> 40), the file whose whole subject is
AASSIGN_COMMON.  Rows 37-39 are the positives, row 40 is the INVERSE (refaddr /
"$r" identity through the copy, class survival, dualvar $! both halves, the #423
glob swap, and refaliasing `\$ra = \$src` still resolving to the referent BOX).
Inverse-verified on the base runtime: exactly 37-39 fail there, 40 passes.
subject: ($x,$y) = ($y,$x) LOSES THE SWAP when the values are REFERENCES -- p-list-= does not snapshot, and the snapshot keeps the live box for a ref
